key_insight: Ultrathin 2D perovskite oxide films can spontaneously break inversion symmetry and generate a tunable out-of-plane bulk photovoltaic effect, exemplified by SrTiO3.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to design next-generation solar and optoelectronic devices with controllable built-in photovoltaic response through thickness, strain, termination, orientation, and twisting.
method: First-principles density functional theory to predict symmetry breaking and BPV response
Tight-binding modeling to capture electronic structure trends in ultrathin films
Symmetry analysis to identify allowed photovoltaic directions and tunability
evidence_signal: The study combines first-principles calculations, tight-binding models, and symmetry arguments to show that 2D ABO3 films naturally exhibit a spontaneous out-of-plane BPV effect.
watch_item: The predicted effect may be highly sensitive to precise film quality, surface termination, and twist/strain control, which could complicate experimental realization.
paper_title: Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Two-Dimensional Perovskite Oxides
